about: What a coach or consultant may change in the Compass design. Protected: the scroll-run topographic map walked from where a client stands to the summit (the fog lifting, three goals as flags, the route planned as a dashed line, the sessions as stops along it, a bridge built over the hard crossing, the glow at the top), the drawn map, the programme cards, the questions that point to a programme, the free-call booking, the monogram, layout, type and all interaction code. The coach's own words, the goals, sessions and weeks, programmes and prices, questions and their scoring, call times and their background come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.
route: the label at the start of the map, three short goals along the way (the last is the summit), how many sessions are drawn as stops, the weeks the programme takes, and the colour of the flags.
log: the four labels beside the map and the word before the week number. stages: six steps in order: where you are, the summit, the route, the sessions, the hard part, the top.

programmes.list: one to three programmes, each with who it's for, a price and what the price is per, sessions and length, what's included, and a line on why the questions might point to it; programmes.badged is the one with the badge (-1 for none).
fit.qs: two to five questions, each with two to four answers; every answer scores each programme (one number per programme, in order) and the highest total is suggested.
call: the times offered each weekday (HH:MM) and the words the booking uses. coach: name, a short background, initials for the monogram and up to four credentials.
